title: sse: streaming framing fixes for partial JSON / delimiter ordering (fixes token/event reordering)
author: Maya Patel
description: Fixes several edge cases in the SSE streaming framing logic that could produce partial/invalid JSON events or reorder token/event boundaries when chunk boundaries coincided with delimiters or multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. Motivation: customers observed intermittent structured-output parse errors and spurious 'partial JSON' blocks while using the OpenAI compatibility streaming endpoint. The root cause was a combination of (1) naive byte-splitting logic that didn't respect multi-byte character boundaries and (2) racey flush + framing behavior that could emit event tokens out of order when the writer boundary hit in the middle of an event. Changes in this PR: add a conservative delimiter-aware buffer, introduce per-stream sequence numbers to preserve event ordering across flushes, ensure UTF-8 safe chunking, add unit/fuzz/integration tests (including a deterministic reproduction harness), update OpenAI-style stream adapter to ensure single-line event semantics, and document the framing guarantees. The description below documents behavioral changes and test coverage. Note: this is a backwards-compatible change for consumers of the OpenAI-style SSE stream (we only make emitted framing more consistent and add explicit ordering metadata for internal correctness).
commits: fix(sse): add delimiter-aware frame buffer and UTF-8 safe chunking
feat(sse): attach sequence numbers to events to enforce ordering across flushes
test(sse): add fuzz tests for delimiter and multi-byte boundary cases
fix(openai-compat): ensure adapter emits single-line SSE events and drops empty delimiters
docs(sse): document framing guarantees and backwards-compat notes
review_comments: Theo Ramirez: Can you add a fuzz test that simulates random chunk boundaries and multi-byte UTF-8 sequences? The old bug was only reproducible with certain boundaries.
Maya Patel: Added fuzz_framing_test.go and a deterministic corpus that reproduces the customer case. Also added a small harness to replay recorded boundary deliveries.
Anika Singh: Please confirm no behavioral change for single-line non-JSON SSE events (we're relying on that in some SDKs).

Maya Patel: Confirmed: the adapter still emits single-line events for non-structured streams. The extra seq header is internal (not surfaced to public event payloads) and only used to guarantee ordering during assembly.
Derek Hollis: Suggest moving the sequence counter to the stream context so it's not shared across multiplexed writers. Also add a metric for reordered events to make regressions visible.
Maya Patel: Reworked seq placement to live in the stream context and added framing_metrics.go with counters for reordered/partial events. Metrics are emitted under 'sse.framing.reorder_count'.

Ensure no cross-stream shared sequence state
author_replies: Implemented fuzz tests and deterministic harness in fuzz_framing_test.go
Moved sequence to stream context and added framing metrics per Derek's suggestion
Addressed lint comments and clarified docs around ordering guarantees
release_notes: Fix: sse streaming framing and partial JSON handling — reduces structured-output parse errors and improves stability of OpenAI-compatible SSE streaming. Includes additional tests and metrics.
notes_for_backport: Low-risk behavioral fix; cherry-pick to release/1.12 recommended for customers on older clusters. Ensure the per-stream seq state is initialized on older server runtime to avoid nil-pointer on backport.
repro_steps: 1) Start local server with OpenAI stream adapter enabled. 2) Run replay harness in serve/sse/fuzz_framing_test.go which feeds events with deliberate chunk splits at UTF-8 boundaries. 3) Before fix, consumer sees partial JSON parse errors or misordered tokens; after fix, events assemble correctly.
behaviour_changes: - Guarantees that tokens/events emitted via SSE preserve original logical ordering even when internal flushes split event content.- Ensures chunking never splits multi-byte UTF-8 sequences.- Adds internal per-stream sequencing; not surfaced in public payloads.- OpenAI compatibility adapter now enforces single-line SSE messages for JSON items and trims empty delimiting lines.
regression_tests: Unit + fuzz + integration; fuzz harness reproducer included as serve/sse/fuzz_corpus/*.gz and run by make test-fuzz. Integration covers real HTTP chunking via http/handler_stream_test.go.
extra_context: This addresses customer-reported SUP-1128 and ties to ENG-3241 (streaming stability) and ENG-3309 (openai-compat regressions). Related prior PRs: pr-91824/pr-89456 which fixed earlier delimiter-edge cases but did not account for multi-byte boundaries.
